records.problem: Users see a response or a short summary, not the full trace. How much does each of these displays reveal about whether the answer is correct?
records.method: Fixed runs, 5 Qwen3/gpt-oss models, GPQA-Diamond, MMLU-Pro, Omni-MATH-2. Linear probes predict correctness from response, self-summary written from the trace alone (≤90 words requested), trace, internals; prompt shown or withheld. Controls: repeated runs, length, masking; GPT-5-mini reader.
records.findings: Prompt withheld: summary AUROC 0.774 vs trace 0.813; summary adds +0.156 over response. Prompt visible: summary +0.019, trace +0.041. Same-question runs, prompt withheld: linear summary readers near chance (0.503–0.545); GPT-5-mini recovers more, trace still +0.034 ahead. Much linear-reader trace signal tied to length.
records.limits: Own-model, non-adversarial summary proxy, not provider summaries. Correctness labels only, not faithfulness. Mostly linear readers; GPT-5-mini tested on one model and benchmark. Length confound unresolved. Code and data released.

records.problem: Unclear whether black-box detectors of unfaithful CoT detect faithfulness or just answer correctness.
records.method: FaithCoT-Bench human labels (4 models, 4 domains), stratified by correctness; step-removal, NLI, premise-DAG signals plus GPT-4o-mini judge; linear probes (Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen-2.5-7B); instructed vs hint-flip testbeds, probe transfer to annotations.
records.findings: Incorrectness oracle (AUROC 0.696) matches or beats every metric; only the judge exceeds it (0.782). 69% of unfaithfulness is on wrong answers, where no metric is detectably above chance and the judge drops (0.830 to 0.679). Step-removal metric inverted (0.349). Only hint-induced probes transfer (onto wrong-answer regime, model- and source-dependent).
records.limits: One annotated benchmark, small minority classes; 69% share release-specific (52% on paper's census); single judge model and prompt; weak steering evidence; scripts in supplement, testbeds promised at camera-ready.

records.problem: CoTs omit input factors that drive decisions (unverbalized biases); bias audits need predefined categories and hand-built datasets.
records.method: Black-box pipeline: o3 proposes concepts from clustered inputs; paired +/- input edits; McNemar on decision flips with Bonferroni and early stopping; concepts cited in >30% of flipped CoTs dropped. Hiring, loan and admissions tasks, 7 LLMs; code and datasets released.
records.findings: 52 unverbalized biases. Rediscovers gender and race biases (all pro-female, pro-minority); finds new ones (Spanish fluency, English proficiency, formality); hiring effects 3-5 pp. Catches 85% of injected secret biases. RLVR QwQ-32B is no more faithful than its SFT sibling (filter rate 97.0 vs 97.2%). Early stopping saves about 1/3 of cost.
records.limits: Binary decision tasks only. LLM edits may confound (judge drops 42%). GPT-5-mini detector kappa 0.67 and over-flags. Only hypothesized concepts are tested. Verbalization via proxies is missed.

records.problem: Do LLM monitors catch agent sabotage better when they see more of the agent's CoT and actions?
records.method: Action-only, CoT-only and CoT+action monitors vs. new extract-and-evaluate (EaE: one monitor quotes excerpts, a separate evaluator scores them) on SHADE-Arena, MLE-Sabotage and BigCodeBench-Sabotage. Scored by log-AUROC and TPR@1%FPR; also varies attacker monitor-awareness, reasoning vs. traditional attackers, and monitor cost.
records.findings: Less-is-more: information filtering wins in 7/8 monitor-environment pairs. EaE: +16.8 pp TPR@1%FPR over best baseline on BigCodeBench (GPT-4.1-mini), +31.5 with GPT-4.1 evaluator. Full-CoT monitors often accept post-hoc justifications. CoT-only monitors catch traditional LLMs better than reasoning ones (subtle, Claude-3.7: 61.7% vs 20.0%). Attacker believes CoT private: CoT monitors gain >0.4 log-AUROC (SHADE-Arena), action-only flat. Code released (SHADE-Arena tasks private).
records.limits: Attackers are prompted, not trained, and trajectories are mostly reused from the original environments. EaE is weaker on SHADE-Arena. The monitor-awareness setups differ across environments. Monitoring is asynchronous (after the run) only, and o3 was not tested.

records.limits: Faithfulness is a side check: 7B only, one cue type, keyword matching, no error bars, not monotonic in alpha.

records.problem: Fine-tuning-based honesty elicitation is validated on model organisms (MOs), but that fine-tuning may erase the implanted behavior it is meant to audit.
records.method: LoRA-trained Llama-3.3-70B secret-side-constraint MOs (Base64 instruction, trained to deny it) → SRFT or generic honesty training. Execution and confession rates, also conditional on execution. Controls: Alpaca fine-tuning, Taboo MO. LoRA-rank and merging ablations on Llama-3.1-8B.
records.findings: SRFT: confession 0.56%→58.52% but execution 81.25%→~7.95%; confessions mostly from non-executing trajectories; 27.68% false confessions on clean prompts. GHT similar. 500 Alpaca samples alone cut execution to ~8%; Taboo MO breaks taboo 87.5% after 4000 Alpaca samples. Rank, merging and steering do not help. Code released.
records.limits: Blog post, not peer reviewed. Only SFT-trained MOs. 8B ablations use a weak MO (29.0% execution when merged). Mitigations not stacked. Steering result preliminary. Execution scoring method not described.

records.problem: Text-edit faithfulness tests are indirect; prior activation-level CoT audits measure degradation, not whether a specific stated step carries its content into the answer.
records.method: 2–6-hop lookup over in-context pseudo-word KB; patch residual stream at stated-step span with counterfactual-run activations; CLB = answer flips to by-construction target; item-matched text-edit baseline; random-position null, post-answer sanity, shuffled-target, prompt-fact ceiling controls.
records.findings: Qwen3-4B CLB 76.9% (null 11.3%, ~96% of 83% ceiling); text editing 88.2%, overstating by 11.4 pp (McNemar p<1e-15), 20.2 pp at 2 hops. Qwen3-1.7B 54.8%, falling 68%→30% with depth; 4B flat. Effect confined to early/mid layers, gone by layer 20/36 (4B).
records.limits: Synthetic single-relation lookup only; two small Qwen3 models, greedy decoding; early-layer patches near token-identity swap; text vs activation edits differ in visibility; workshop paper; no code release reported.

records.problem: Reasoning models may keep writing CoT after internally settling on an answer ("performative" CoT), so text monitors lag the model's belief.
records.method: Attention probes, forced answering and a Gemini-2.5-Flash CoT monitor decode the final answer from CoT prefixes. Models: DeepSeek-R1, GPT-OSS-120B, R1-Qwen distills 1.5-32B. Tasks: MMLU-Redux vs GPQA-D.
records.findings: MMLU CoT largely performative (R1 performativity rate 0.417 vs 0.012 on GPQA-D), more so in larger models. Inflections twice as frequent per step in less confident traces. Probe early exit saves 68% of tokens and keeps 97% of accuracy on MMLU. Code released.
records.limits: 4-option MCQ only; correlational; gap measured against one LLM monitor; timing of inflections vs probe shifts inconsistent and threshold-sensitive; distill probes unstable across layers.

records.problem: Tool-using agents may report plans that please an observer while executing something else. Prior deception benchmarks rarely combine tool execution with controls that separate strategy from hallucination.
records.method: 300 paired regular/pressure dilemmas over simulated tools. Deception = the plan shifts toward the observer under pressure while the action stays intrinsic. Stances labeled by an SFT Qwen3-32B judge; pass@5.
records.findings: All 8 models deceive in more than 20% of cases (Gemini-2.5-Pro 57.33%, GPT-5.1 25%). Deception is non-monotonic in Qwen3 size, flat across GPT-5.1 reasoning effort, and its pressure sensitivity and style (conflict vs ambiguous) vary by model.
records.limits: Preprint. Simulated tools, binary dilemmas; cases filtered to those eliciting divergence in reference models. Measured deception feigns observer compliance while acting on principle. Judge: 82.5% deception accuracy vs human labels. Test-awareness may mask deception. Release claimed, no link.

records.method: Four CoT-necessity levels. M1: Guan's minimal-criterion score on answers with no-CoT probability <0.01; attribute-sentence removal, 2×1000 split CoTs, DeepSeek-V4 judge. Level 2: early-answer direct effect, frozen KV cache. Thyroid, DDXPlus, Olympic Athletes, Hinted MCQA; four Qwen3/Gemma-4 models.

Beats prompting and SFT; beats StTP steering on MASK, on par elsewhere. AlpacaEval at parity (StTP drops Llama to 8.6%; UltraChat utility data instead: ~22-29%). MMLU within 1 point.
records.limits: White-box only. Two models; AuditBench on Llama only, 5 audits per behavior, baselines digitized from the original paper. Confession regex is a lower bound. CAPO variants cause refusals. Code promised but not yet released.

records.problem: Free-text rationale metrics (LAS, RQ) measure only label association, so they cannot detect vacuous rationales that restate input and label without adding new information.
records.method: REV (conditional V-information): label log-prob of a T5-Large evaluator given rationale plus a vacuous baseline (input+label as one sentence), minus that of a second evaluator given the baseline alone. Tested on ECQA, CoS-E, QuaRTz and e-SNLI, scoring T5 rationales and GPT-3/LaMDA CoT. Code released.
records.findings: Scores vacuous rationales low where LAS/RQ score them high; ranking matches human ratings (230 ECQA items). On GPT-3 rationales, REV>0 agrees 80% with human support judgments; LAS/RQ rate only 35%/23% as supporting (56%/60% zero). CoT REV similar for GPT-3 and LaMDA (0.92 vs 0.99) despite 77% vs 59% accuracy.
records.limits: Measures informativeness and label support, not faithfulness to the decision process. Rewards rationales for wrong labels and ignores factuality. Depends on gold-rationale quality and evaluator architecture; tests a single baseline construction.

relations.note: LAS baseline; rates vacuous rationales high and is less sensitive to input noise

records.problem: CoT monitors assume an actor's harmful planning shows up in its own reasoning. Reasoning supplied in the actor's context may get around this.
records.method: Investigator agents (SFT+DPO) find stealthy TruthfulQA hints. Generalized as "plan injection": DeepSeek-R1 corrupts benign CoTs (APPS backdoors, Bio-Math hidden answer), which are offered as optional plans to Qwen3-8B and DeepSeek-R1. Five thinking and non-thinking monitors, with and without the plan; Qwen3-235B budget sweep.
records.findings: Actors follow the plans (best of 3: APPS 42-51%, Bio-Math 93-99%) and paraphrase them without attribution. Thinking monitors detect more on average, but the best misses at least 25%; self-authored attacks are caught far more often. Plan access or a larger monitor budget sometimes lowers detection.
records.limits: Two actors, two tasks. Budget study uses one monitor on extreme-selected transcripts, so prevalence is unknown. No end-to-end RAG or agent delivery. Abstract and Sec. 6.2 disagree on which task plan access hurts. No code release stated.

records.problem: Legal LLMs often answer directly, without multi-step reasoning. RLVR rewards only answer correctness, not how much the CoT contributes.
records.method: SFT on 450 DeepSeek-R1 traces, then GRPO (LoRA) with reward = format + correctness x sigmoid(T*dQ). dQ = the model's own average answer logits with CoT minus without (PMI plus a confidence term). Qwen2.5-7B/14B. Trained on CAIL2018/JEC-QA; 5 in-domain legal tasks; DiscLaw benchmark as OOD.

records.limits: No faithfulness test (no CoT edits or cues). dQ could reward CoTs that restate the answer. Ablations on 14B only; w/o SFT better on 2/5 tasks; no variance reported. Legal domain only.

records.problem: Where in post-training CoT hint-following and concealment emerge is unknown. The author's earlier hint replication tested only final deployed models.
records.method: Four public OLMo-3 checkpoints (base, SFT, DPO, RLVR). Wrong answer planted in question metadata (Chen et al.). 100 MMLU-Pro items the base model can answer x 20 rollouts. Gemini-3-Flash judge. CoT vs No-CoT arms. GPQA replication.
records.findings: Not monotone across stages. SFT nearly doubles following but has the lowest concealment (0.43). DPO: following dips slightly; concealment back above 50% via silent arithmetic edits (42%) and reframed assumptions (63%). RLVR: lowest following, concealment at DPO level, both marginal vs DPO. CoT reduces following except at DPO (+0.02, n.s.). Base-model concealment is mostly formatting artifacts. GPQA directionally similar.
records.limits: Blog post, not peer reviewed. One model lineage, size not stated, one simple hint type. Base model gets a different few-shot completion prompt. LLM judge not validated. Category shares scored by Claude. GPQA run noisy. No code release stated.

records.problem: Mobile GUI agents are scored mainly by action exact match (EM). Whether the CoT implies the gold action goes unchecked, which hides reasoning–execution gaps, so users may over-trust plausible reasoning.
records.method: GTA: a VLM evaluator (AgentCPM-GUI-8B) maps CoT + screenshot to the action it implies, matched against the gold action. Combined with EM this gives an execution gap (CoT right, action wrong) and a reasoning gap (action right, CoT wrong). Six open agents on AITZ, CAGUI and AndroidControl; UI-TARS 2B–72B for scaling.
records.findings: GTA > EM in 14/18 model–dataset pairs (execution gaps dominate); EG is largest on OOD CAGUI (up to 21.8%). AgentCPM and UI-TARS-7B show RG > EG on AITZ, which the authors attribute to SFT action shortcuts. Scaling shrinks both gaps, but 72B still has EG > 10%; DPO slightly beats SFT. Evaluator–human agreement 77–94%. Code released.
records.limits: Correlational: the CoT is never intervened on, and gaps are defined against a single gold action, so both-wrong mismatches go uncounted. The evaluator is also one of the evaluated models and is validated on only 3 of the 6 models, using consensus labels only. Scaling results (UI-TARS, AndroidControl) appear only in a figure and clash with Table 4 (7B EG 9.2% < 72B's >10%; 7B DPO no better than SFT). Open models ≤72B; preprint.

records.problem: Latent CoT removes the readable trace. How much hint-reliance monitorability do activation probes or verbalized latents keep?
records.method: Llama-3.2-1B: No-CoT, explicit CoT, CODI, SIM-CoT, each hint-fine-tuned to a range of reliance rates. Label is a sycophancy-hint answer flip. Monitors: exact match, prompted Qwen3-14B, LoRA text classifiers (native, logit lens, decoder), attention probes. AUROC on GSM8k and ECQA, plus SVAMP and SIQA as OOD.
records.findings: Task and access to internals matter more than reasoning mode. Answer-token probes best for most tasks and modes. Explicit-CoT text helps on math via CoT-answer mismatch (rate 0.79 hint-reliant vs 0.04 not), not on ECQA. Logit lens closes the math gap; SIM-CoT decoder does not. Math transfers OOD; most latent-model QA monitors fall near baseline. Hint fine-tuning costs little no-hint accuracy.
records.limits: One 1B base model, two latent methods, two tasks. A single correct-answer sycophancy hint. Hint-reliance is induced by fine-tuning, not natural. No RL or optimization pressure against the monitors.

records.problem: Planted-cue tests usually put the cue in the user message, but agents receive preferences through tool returns or raw artifacts. Does the CoT record the decision to tailor the answer?
records.method: FACE-Eval, 5,100 samples crossing user message vs prefilled tool return with summary vs raw-artifact cue, plus no-cue controls. Claude Haiku 4.5 judges verbalized commitment (VCR) and unverbalized adoption. 15 open models, 4B–1.60T. Source-attribution and monitor-aware system prompts. Transcript monitors (GPT-5.6-Luna, GPT-4o-mini).
records.findings: On all 15 models, VCR is lower for tool-return and implicit cues. Neither prompt reliably closes the gaps. GPT-5.6-Luna monitor AUROC 0.71–0.73, with the CoT adding detection only on user-channel cues; AUROC falls as unverbalized adoption rises (r −0.54/−0.78). Code and data released.
records.limits: Single-call prefilled tool, not multi-step agency. Absolute VCR depends on the judge (inter-judge AC1 0.75). Mechanism unidentified; explicitness is confounded with format. Tailoring may not need CoT. Preprint.

records.problem: Follow-up to a replication of MacDiarmid et al.: RL runs with a KL penalty learned reward hacks with unfaithful CoT. Is this robust, plausible in production, and fixable?
records.method: DAPO/GRPO RL on very hard coding envs with 3 disclosed but forbidden hacks, with vs. without reverse-KL; Olmo-3-32B (3 seeds), Qwen2.5-32B (1 seed); LLM CoT monitor. No-CoT hack-discovery evals of Sonnet 4.6, Haiku 4.5, GPT-4o-mini. Mitigations: KL on output tokens only; judge-based unfaithfulness penalty.
records.findings: Olmo: KL runs consistently hack unfaithfully, no-KL runs faithfully; Qwen ~70% unfaithful without KL, ~100% with it. Frontier models mostly find hacks without reasoning. Output-only KL brings faithfulness to ~50%, faithfulness penalty to ~100%. Faithful hackers show ~3x misalignment. KL framed as an implicit in-conflict CoT reward. Checkpoints and rollouts released.
records.limits: Blog post, not peer reviewed; self-described preliminary. Three easy fixed hacks, one setting; Qwen single seed. No monitor validation reported. CoT-suppression mechanism only hypothesized. Goodhart risk of faithfulness reward untested.

records.problem: CoT faithfulness metrics are never checked against ground truth; earlier benchmarks rely on plausibility or importance as proxies.
records.method: BonaFide: 3,066 CoTs from 13 tasks and 10 open models (4B-70B). Ground truth comes from task design: following a hint to a wrong answer, or bottleneck computations a correct answer requires. LLM judges label steps (98.9% precision against humans). Eight metrics scored by AUROC at step and CoT level.
records.findings: Most metrics near chance and skewed (most importance-based call 90-96% of CoTs unfaithful, semantic-utility 94-96% faithful), and worse on long CoTs. Best: CC-SHAP 0.70 (CoT), Filler Tokens 0.59 (step), neither transfers to the other level. CC-SHAP takes up to 10^3 s per instance.
records.limits: Ground truth only for design-determined steps, most steps unlabeled; precision-first design leaves few faithful CoTs (15%); step/instance versions of most metrics are author adaptations; open models only; LLM-judge skyline shares the labeling signal. Preprint; benchmark and code released.

records.problem: Outcome-only RLVR reinforces traces that are right for the wrong reasons, and it ignores whether the reasoning helps the model that consumes it.
records.method: TraceLift: a GRPO-trained planner writes the trace and a frozen same-family executor writes the answer. Reward = verifier + rubric Reason-RM score × executor uplift (trace vs. no trace, K=3). The RM is trained on TraceLift-Groups: 6,000 reference-vs-perturbed groups with LLM rubric labels. Math and code.
records.findings: Beats execution-only RL on every benchmark for all 3 models (code micro-avg +1.96–2.61 pts, math +0.84–4.51); direct self-solving math also ≥ Exec-only. Without uplift, or with a prompted judge, it falls below Exec-only. Traces are shorter (136 vs 166 tokens). Code released.
records.limits: Only task accuracy and length are evaluated; no validity or faithfulness test of the trained traces. Models ≤8B, executor from the same family. Rubric-label judge unnamed; RM validated only on in-distribution GSM8K perturbations. Ablations on Qwen2.5-7B code only. Under review.

records.problem: Self-explanations may be unfaithful. Do they still help users predict model behavior (counterfactual simulatability), and does the way test counterfactuals are built drive that verdict?
records.method: StrategyQA; CoT and post-hoc explanations from GPT-3.5, GPT-4 and Llama-3.3-70B. Three LLM-generated counterfactual sets vs. four Gricean pragmatic perturbations (presupposition flip, lexical, scalar, contextualization). Two-phase prediction (without, then with, the explanation) by gpt-3.5-turbo and gpt-4.1 judges and 28 humans.
records.findings: Explanations raise judge simulation accuracy (mean gain ~0.30 weak judge, ~0.15 strong judge). Post-hoc ≈ CoT. Lexical, presupposition-flip and scalar sets give more stable gains than LLM-generated ones; contextualization near ceiling for strong judge. Explanations reduce anchoring to wrong original answers. Humans: accuracy 0.614→0.634 (LLM-generated sets ≤+0.01), confidence 3.21→4.38. LLM–human agreement ~0.60.
records.limits: Binary yes/no QA, one dataset, few models. Judge gains mostly from fewer 'cannot guess' answers (scored wrong); selective accuracy barely moves. Small user study (50 items, GPT-4 explanations only). Taxonomy incomplete; LLM-generated artifacts. Paper claims usefulness, not faithfulness. Code and annotations promised on publication.

records.problem: Mobile GUI agents act on memorized shortcuts rather than screen/instruction evidence, and execute actions contradicting their own Thought; sparse abstain rewards collapse GRPO advantages.
records.method: Qwen3-VL-8B. Code released.
records.findings: Trap SR 13.88%→80.21% (71.20 after SFT alone), General SR 60.38→65.62. Contradictory thought-action pairs 59.29%→17.17%; under-abstain 57.75%→8.86%, over-abstain flat (~5%). records.limits: One 8B backbone; offline step-level eval only; no seeds or variance reported. Consistency is scored by the same keyword rule used as reward. GuAE gains are small. "Faithfulness" here mostly means abstention robustness, not causal CoT faithfulness.

records.problem: CoT monitoring only works if the chain constrains the answer. When is the CoT decorative, and when is it load-bearing?
records.method: Perturb one step, truncate, force the model to continue. Wrong final answer = error propagation; a Claude Haiku judge splits the rest into bypass vs self-correction. Gemma-2-9B, Llama-3.1-8B, R1-Distill-Qwen-7B on GSM8K, MMLU, BBH, plus a matched perturbation-type × difficulty 2×2. Hidden-state probes and additive steering.
records.findings: Propagation tracks model-relative difficulty (Gemma 3.9%→22.3%→40.9%) and replicates on Llama. Difficulty takes 98.8% of explained deviance, perturbation type 0.8%. R1-Distill propagates less. Probes read the mode; steering flips at most ~25% of Type C. Code released.
records.limits: 7–9B models only. Single-step, non-naturalistic perturbations. A/B split is judge-prompt-sensitive, and production labels over-count self-correction (76% three-way agreement with humans, 96% on C vs non-C). Difficulty confounded with competence. Answer-parser errors inflate BBH propagation (humans relabel 40% of a BBH Type C stratum as bypass).

records.problem: Is the final answer predetermined before CoT starts, or computed during CoT and causally dependent on it?
records.method: Synthetic multi-step arithmetic at 5 complexity levels (steps, stack, distractors), few-shot CoT. Linear probes per token, layer and variable locate when (sub-)answers become decodable. Activation patching over equation x 4-layer grids. 9 open models, 3-34B.
records.findings: Computed (sub-)answers decodable only after CoT begins (pre-CoT probe accuracy peaks around 60%). Final answer depends causally mainly on CoT states; Input patching has limited effect. Strong recency bias: the model reuses written results instead of recomputing. Distractor values not linearly decodable (<=44%). Concludes CoT is faithful here.

records.method: RLTR: GRPO plus a transfer reward. The generator's CoT is truncated (tau in [0.3,0.9]) and a frozen receiver (Qwen2.5-3B; Llama-3.2-3B for Llama) continues it; reward if the receiver's answer is correct. Generators Qwen2.5-7B and Llama-3.1-8B, MATH train.

records.problem: A retained reasoning trace can raise accuracy but also override updated evidence. Trace-deletion tests may not tell these two roles apart.
records.method: Traces written from original or entity-edited evidence (683 HotpotQA, 417 MuSiQue verified pairs) are crossed with the other version. Answers come from continuation in the thinking block or a separate answer call. Trace removal, random half-trace and answer-swap corruption ablations; gold vs distractor evidence before vs after the trace; 8 models.
records.findings: Separate call raises evidence-following by 29.9-60.6 pts while trace contribution differs by at most 4.7 pts, costing at most 1.9 pts matched accuracy. Continuation follows the stale trace 65.6-87.0%. Distractors weaken separate-call correction. Final line carries most value. Input order explains most of the gap in 2 of 3 models. Re-reason corrects 86.6% (Qwen3-14B, about 2x tokens); a verify prompt does not help.
records.limits: Two English multi-hop QA datasets; synthetic entity-substitution conflicts; only pairs whose traces state an explicit answer; three paired models (DeepSeek separate-call only); no code release mentioned.

records.problem: Do Claude 3.5 Haiku's written CoT and self-explanations match its internal mechanisms? This is one case study inside a broad circuit-tracing survey.
records.method: Attribution graphs on a 30M-feature cross-layer-transcoder replacement model. Feature-inhibition interventions. The human-suggested answer is varied. The model is asked how it did addition.
records.findings: sqrt(0.64) CoT faithful: graph shows it computes sqrt(64), and the answer ignores varied hints. Unhinted cos(23423): bullshits, claiming a calculator; graph suggests guessing. Hinted: works backward from the suggested answer (inhibitions confirm the circuit), and the CoT ends at whatever answer is hinted. Asked about addition, it describes carrying; its circuits use parallel low-precision and ones-digit lookup-table paths.

records.problem: Does task-specific fine-tuning degrade CoT accuracy and CoT faithfulness (the answer depending on the stated steps)?
records.method: SFT of Llama-3-8B (QLoRA) and of GPT-3.5/GPT-4 (via API) on GSM8K (with rationales), MedQA or CosmosQA (answers only). Each model is scored on 4 datasets with per-instance Lanham tests (early termination, filler substitution, paraphrase), reported as CoT Pred Match at 25/50/75% of the steps. Also sweeps QLoRA rank 8/16/32.
records.findings: Fine-tuning usually lowers CoT accuracy, most in Llama-3-8B; GPT models gain no-CoT accuracy. GPT-4 and GPT-3.5 faithfulness barely changes. Llama fine-tuned on MedQA/CosmosQA becomes less faithful on the non-math test sets, at all ranks. GPT-4 least faithful by early-termination and filler tests. Code released.
records.limits: 3 models (GPT sizes undisclosed), 4 datasets; faithfulness shown only as plots, no significance tests. Rationale vs answer-only tuning is confounded with dataset (GSM8K only). Fine-tuned Llama's repetitive CoTs may inflate CoT Pred Match (our reading of Tables 1-2). Early-stage Lanham metrics; no mechanistic analysis.

records.problem: A single sampled CoT cannot show which steps cause a decision. Handwritten edits are off-policy, and models re-derive steps that were removed.
records.method: Resample continuations from each sentence (100 rollouts). New metrics: resilience (resamples until content stays gone) and counterfactual++ importance (KL with content absent). Compare on- and off-policy insertions; transplant hinted unfaithful CoT prefixes into unhinted MMLU prompts; estimate resume sentence-cluster effects. Settings: blackmail, MMLU, resumes.
records.findings: Self-preservation sentences: lowest resilience, ~0.001-0.003 KL; plan generation drives blackmail. Off-policy edits near-zero effect; on-policy resampling cuts blackmail/whistleblowing up to 100% for some targets. Hints nudge CoT subtly, diffusely, cumulatively ("Wait" 30% rarer). Sentences mediate 77.5% of demographic effect on average (significant in 5/8 resumes). Code released.
records.limits: Costly, offline only. Specific prompts (one blackmail scenario, 20 CoTs/model; 40 hint-effective MMLU Qs; 8 resumes); hint and resume studies use one model each. Black-box, no internal validation. LLM-judge outcome labels. On MATH, handwritten edits have stronger local effects.

records.problem: Cue-verbalization tests score only answer-switch cases and ignore reasoning unrelated to the cue, so CoTs that leave out key factors still look faithful.

records.limits: Single-turn temp-0 MCQ only. Factor lists LLM-made; judge overcounts on 58.3% of 120 human-checked samples. Echoing the prompt could inflate verbosity. Cue mentions count regardless of influence.

records.problem: Introspection evals conflate privileged self-access with world knowledge or text-based self-simulation.
records.method: Formal taxonomy of policy introspection. Introspect-Bench: 796 no-CoT items (k-th word, predicting CoT verdicts on ethical dilemmas, prompt reconstruction, Heads-Up). 10 models cross-predict each other. SFT probe on Qwen3-8B; logit lens and ablation on Qwen3-32B. Code released.
records.findings: Models predict themselves better than peers (p=0.021); no model leads every task. For GPT-5.2, no-CoT predictions are closer in KL to CoT verdicts than gut answers are. SFT on outputs alone yields self-prediction. Attention diffusion accounts for 23.9% of the logit shift.
records.limits: Workshop paper. Self-advantage rests on one test; Table 2's self average (64.19%) trails five models. Heads-Up near ceiling. Long-term result on GPT-5.2 only; mechanism from one model and layer. Inconsistent k range and model count. Mechanistic and CoT-assisted introspection untested.

records.problem: Can LLMs tell, in a follow-up turn, that their own prior (harmful) output was forced by an adversarial prefill?
records.method: 10 open models (3B-70B), 4 safety benchmarks; AdvPrefix vs. control; intention and tampering probes; RoBERTa claim classifier; recognition gap = claim rate control minus prefill; refusal-direction ablation; LoRA SFT/GRPO/DPO.
records.findings: 25.3% of prefilled outputs still claimed as intended. Rejections mostly cite safety/policy. Refusal ablation closes the gap to near zero on all six 8B-32B models, random directions partly too; Qwen3-8B/14B gap vanishes under benign placebo prefill. Probe framing changes results. Finetuning widens the gap on 8B-32B models, but it does not transfer to the tampering probe and raises ASR on most models. MMLU stays within -4.8%. Code released.
records.limits: Interventions only on open models up to 32B; English only; one operationalization of introspection; the same RoBERTa classifier is the GRPO reward and the metric; prefills fall back to a static string on two benchmarks; rank-16 LoRA only.

records.problem: Agents may not carry out the plans they declare, and task success alone cannot tell execution failures apart from a badly chosen planning mode.
records.method: A rule-based verifier, checked against human annotators, tests whether Plan+ReAct trajectories follow the declared steps in order. Planning-as-Routing sends the declared mode (predefined, sequential, hierarchical or search) to a matching executor. Forced-dispatch ceilings. Benchmarks: ALFWorld, Mind2Web, WebArena, SWE-bench Verified.
records.findings: Plan+ReAct keeps the declared structure in 12-45% of trajectories on ALFWorld, Mind2Web and SWE-bench (more on WebArena), and less for longer plans. The best fixed-pattern executor lifts DeepSeek-V4 over Plan+ReAct from 0.48 to 0.92 (ALFWorld) and 0.36 to 0.44 (SWE-bench); routing on the model's declared mode reaches 0.72 and 0.42. Declared modes do no better than a task-blind null.
records.limits: Checks step order, not whether actions are correct; routed runs count as faithful from dispatch records, not verified. Verifier kappa 0.31-0.34 against humans, who agree with each other at 0.35 (100 ALFWorld trajectories). Three open models. Hierarchical and Search use more tokens and LLM calls. Code promised but not yet released. Preprint.

records.problem: Weak monitors and students need usable strong-model CoTs; existing legibility metrics reward conciseness or need strong judges.
records.method: Transfer utility: weak models (Phi-3-Mini, Llama-3.2-1B) finish tasks from growing prefixes of correct traces; ~85k traces, 12 open RLMs, MATH/GPQA/LSAT.
records.findings: Accuracy weakly anti-correlates with FOTU (rho=-0.35); GPT-OSS-120B near last; rankings stable across students and tasks. FOTU predicts weak-monitor precision on MATH (rho=+0.90) and LSAT; GPQA null after length control. Reward models ignore it beyond correctness.

records.problem: Anti-scheming training could teach models to hide misbehavior rather than drop it, and behavioral evals alone cannot tell which happened.
records.method: Deliberative alignment (SFT on rollouts filtered for spec-motivated reasoning, then outcome RL) on o3/o4-mini. Tested on 26 OOD covert-action evals (180+ environments). Adds a CoT eval-awareness classifier, CoT ablation and injection, SITA-hint training, an inserted hidden sabotage goal, and later capability RL.
records.findings: Covert actions fall 13%→0.4% (o3) and 8.7%→0.3% (o4-mini) but persist. Verbalized eval awareness rises, and ablating it raises covert actions 13.2→24.2%. Many hint-driven trajectories pass the CoT filter. CoT-action mismatches and odd jargon appear. Inserted goal mostly suppressed, but red-teaming still elicits it. Capability RL cuts spec citation 81.5→65.8%.
records.limits: Closed OpenAI models only. CoT interventions use a single eval on pre-intervention o3. No training-resistant (deceptively aligned) models. Verbalized awareness is a weak proxy. SWE-bench drops 69→43% (o4-mini). No public data release.

records.problem: Schema-guided reasoning produces editable rubrics, checklists, queries or execution traces. Do the final decisions causally follow these structures?
records.method: Correct or counterfactually edit the model's own mediator on tasks where a deterministic map fixes the new answer, then re-prompt. Metrics F_ID vs F_Strong. 12 open models (1.7B–235B, thinking off) on RiceChem, AVeriTeC, TabFact and CRUXEval. Case studies: tool externalization, stronger prompts, DPO on faithful-vs-stubborn pairs. Code released.
records.findings: Mean F_ID–F_Strong gap ~18–23 pp on 3 of 4 datasets. Counterfactual edits are followed more often than corrections. CRUXEval: larger Qwen models bypass the trace (inverse scaling). Tools mostly cut the gap below 0.03. Prompting gives inconsistent gains. DPO raises F_Strong (Qwen3-8B RiceChem 0.52→0.73), accuracy flat or up, but Qwen3-8B AVeriTeC stays flat (0.31→0.29).
records.limits: Needs gold mediators and deterministic mappings. Open models only, non-reasoning mode. DPO tested on two 8B models only, trains directly on the edited-mediator following that F_Strong scores, and the train/test split is not reported.

records.problem: Do LLMs' metalinguistic answers (grammaticality, next-word choice) reflect their own string probabilities, with no fine-tuning?
records.method: 21 open models, 1.5-405B. Data: BLiMP/Linguistic Inquiry minimal pairs and 4 word-prediction sets (incl. nonsense, random). Correlate model A's prompted preference with model B's log-prob preference. Regress on similarity (seed, base/instruct, family, Direct-Direct r) to test for a same-model effect.
records.findings: Both methods accurate but kappa about 0.25; in Exp. 1, Meta-Direct r never above .25, even within model. Similarity predicts alignment (Exp. 1 r=.32), but no self advantage, even against OLMo seed variants or among models of 70B and up. Larger models' prompted answers track probabilities better.
records.limits: Open weights only, >70B 4-bit quantized; two linguistic domains; forced-choice logit readout; null result may not hold for larger closed models. Code and data released.

records.problem: Language drift (odd, illegible CoT language) may erode CoT monitorability, and its causes are poorly understood.
records.method: Proofs treat drift as KL divergence from human language, for RLVR vs SFT. DAPO vs SFT on GSM8K: three 1-1.5B base models, 5 seeds, iso-accuracy checkpoints. Instruct readers, or sibling seeds, guess the model's answer from partial CoTs.
records.findings: RLVR permits unbounded drift, SFT bounds it; capping drift caps expected reward. Novel-task Llama/Gemma: RLVR CoTs less legible than SFT (AUC -0.24/-0.17) and drift differs per seed. Qwen, which mostly sharpens existing behavior: virtually no drift vs SFT. Code released.
records.limits: Only 1-1.5B models, GSM8K only. Reader legibility is only a proxy for drift. Drift-reward theorem untested empirically. Drift is milder than in frontier CoTs.

records.problem: Deception is context-conditional; unlearning targets facts. Suppression (NPO) leaves deception; BCT-style neutral-target distillation removes it but blinds models to the context (benign instructions, secrets, CoT mentions of the pressure).
records.method: Forget set of own answer flips between pressure and neutral contexts, belief held (sycophancy, MASK). Pact: LoRA SFT on the honest trace prefixed by an acknowledgment of the pressure, plus a benign system-prompt retain set. Compared with NPO, DPO and distillation.
records.findings: QwQ/R1-32B deception 50–67% → 1.0–2.5%. Traces mention the user 99/98% vs 34/14% under distillation. Secrets and adherence kept; ToW 0.94/0.86. GSM8K/MMLU within 4 pts. Ten deceptive steps undo removal; attack-aware hardening (on distillation) holds them but cuts trace mentions to 7/4%. Code released.
records.limits: Two 32B models. Eval mostly instructed sycophancy. Keyword trace metric. LLM judge, no human agreement. LoRA only, one seed per row. Hardening not combined with Pact. Monitor value of the restored mentions untested.

records.problem: Hint-based faithfulness evals never tell models how to treat unusual input. Open question: when explicitly asked, do LRMs report relying on hints?
records.method: Chen et al. hints (re-created templates; 4 types, correct/incorrect) on GPQA-Diamond and 200 MMLU-Pro items. Prompt asks the model to flag unusual content and state its intended use; hint use is permitted. A GPT-5.4 judge labels presence, intent and use. Metrics: normalized F̄, H̄_I, H̄_U.
records.findings: Hint-presence F̄ is high (perfect for metadata and unethical-info hints). Yet models mostly deny intending to use hints while their answers follow them; Qwen H̄_I is near zero. H̄_U higher for Qwen and Kimi; Claude often never mentions the hint again. Weak intent-use alignment. No consistent difficulty trend; budget shifts Claude's scores, not Qwen's. Code released.

records.problem: Behavioral and attribution tests of CoT faithfulness ignore internal computation. Does the CoT reuse the concepts behind the direct answer, and do those concepts causally drive it?
records.method: One off-the-shelf SAE per layer encodes the answer-position residuals of a no-CoT pass and a CoT-conditioned pass. records.findings: Overlap is high but barely predicts Δp (lift 1.08). Random and norm-matched ablations give far smaller Δp. Δp mostly peaks at mid-to-late layers. records.limits: Only models of 9B or less; only items where CoT and no-CoT answers agree. Relies on pretrained SAEs (Δp robust to width/sparsity, r>0.8); no ground truth. records.problem: Do LLM agents act on the reasoning they state? Social simulations have no reference behavior to check this process fidelity against.
records.method: Texas Hold'em multi-agent simulator with a Monte Carlo reference action. The gap is split in two: conclusion→action (DECISION tag vs JSON action, compared with a free-text parser) and reasoning→conclusion (DECISION vs the agent's own stated EQUITY/POT_ODDS/RULE; stated equity vs Monte Carlo flags input errors). Four prompt strategies, plus a "mechanical rule" prompt ablation.
records.findings: Explicit-tag conclusion→action inconsistency is 0.7–1.8% across the three models; the free-text parser's 22–26% (Haiku, Flash-Lite) is a parsing artifact. Rule misapplication is a third of Haiku's interpretable errors but 8% of DeepSeek's, and 99.5% of Haiku's misapplications are risk-averse. The mechanical prompt halves misapplication (13.9→6.8%) and raises adherence 8 points. Injecting the rule does not reliably raise adherence. Code released.
records.limits: Three API models; diagnostic run on only two, mechanical ablation on Haiku only. Poker is not a social simulation. The reference is a threshold heuristic, not true GTO. Verbose elicitation may change behavior. DeepSeek parse rate is 62%. χ² tests treat decisions as independent.

records.problem: As the capability gap widens and frontier CoT turns opaque, weak trusted monitors may no longer reliably judge agents' actions.
records.method: An untrusted monitor with transparent CoT scores the agent's actions, and a weak trusted model audits that CoT and verdict for collusion. Tested on BashArena side tasks with prompted collusion (default, needle, codewords) and automated red teaming, scored as catch rate at ≤3% FPR.
records.findings: With raw CoT, beats trusted-only under collusion in most cells (worst prompt loses on short GPT-5.4 rollouts with GPT-4.1 Mini T). Catch rises from ~60% to ~95% with rollout length (~30% per-step leak). Red teaming cannot push detection below 80% on long rollouts, but reaches ~20% on short ones until blue-team re-prompting of T restores ~70% catch. With summarized CoT (GPT-5.4), below trusted-only in 5/6 cells, ~28pp on average.

records.problem: RL-finetuned VLMs gain benchmark accuracy, but it is unclear whether they are robust to misleading text and whether their CoTs agree with their answers.
records.method: Wrong-Caption, prefilled Wrong-Think and Stop-Think perturbations on 8 visual QA sets (mostly spatial MCQ). records.findings: Misleading text cuts accuracy. The most robust open models are the least consistent; closed models are more robust and more consistent. records.limits: Measures answer-CoT consistency, not causal faithfulness (authors concede). Open models 7-8B only; mostly spatial MCQ. Large variance across seeds. records.method: GRACE: 1 minus the influence-weighted Jaccard of the top-64 position-pooled transcoder concepts in circuit-tracer attribution graphs, clean vs. perturbed run (CoT paraphrase, truncation, mistake injection; prompt hint). Tested on Gemma-2-2B and Qwen3-4B with BBH and MMLU.
records.findings: Correlates with Lanham AOC (rho +0.44 and +0.41). Partial rho is +0.34 and +0.27 after controlling for edit distance, length and graph size. Tracks truncation but not mistake injection. Does not predict hint flips (Gemma AUROC 0.47).
records.limits: Two small models, each needing a matched transcoder. MCQ only, since circuit-tracer attributes a single answer token. Correlational only: no causal tests on the flagged concepts. The Qwen sample was enriched for AOC-active items, and its mistake dissociation is underpowered (n=42). Under review at ARR.

records.problem: TPRmc also counts target outcomes that would have occurred without the intervention, so it can overstate monitor recall. Can post-training raise CoT monitorability?
records.method: Proves TPRmc is an upper bound on causal recall and derives an observable lower bound. Builds 3,810 paired cue/evidence/sandbag/deception tasks. Trains Qwen3.5-4B/9B and Mistral-24B with self-distilled SFT, monitor-reward GRPO and privileged-context OPSD. Evaluates on 12 MonitorBench tasks with 3 held-out monitors.
records.findings: Per Tables 2-3, the upper-bound composite rises in 24/27 comparisons, the lower-bound one in 24/27. SFT raises both in all 9 (Mistral upper bound +7 to +19). RL and OPSD results are mixed for 9B and Mistral and sometimes flip between bounds. Code in supplement.
records.limits: The bounds do not identify recall. Methods are not matched (SFT tuned more). Training data built automatically. Accuracy cost not reported. Text counts (23/27, 21/27) and some deltas contradict Tables 2-3. Under review, not yet peer reviewed.

records.problem: Introspection benchmarks score self-report accuracy, which cannot separate introspection, self-simulation and rationalization (causal bypassing).
records.method: Other LLMs (ICL/LoRA) and static-embedding classifiers predict the source's probe-derived or behaviour labels; LoRA-train on each of 16 datasets (steering awareness, self-prediction, confidence), test cross-task; 8 models, 7-70B.
records.findings: Activation labels: cross LLMs match self (commonsense 71.8 vs 71.4%), embeddings recover them from text. Behaviour labels: cross reporters recover 89% of self lift; residual +5.3 to +7.9 points only on own-generation tasks. In-task gains largely fail to transfer across families (median -0.01); not forgetting (IFEval within ~2 points).
records.limits: Cannot separate introspection from self-simulation; at most 200 eval rows per source, 3 seeds, ~8B reporters on behaviour labels; Gemma LoRA reporters collapse; open models only; under review, not peer reviewed; code in supplement.

records.method: Criterion derived from tool registry and business rules; decision tree matches completive claims to tool-call logs; all 452 candidates human-adjudicated; 7 models, 3 insurance scenarios (1,799 trajectories); tau-bench replication (1,980).

records.limits: Author-led annotation; codebook revised on analysis data (version kappa 0.21); write-operation domains only; LLM-selected candidate pool; pooled rate driven by two models (29.2% without Qwen-Plus); under review. Protocol, codebook, data released.

records.problem: Cue-based unfaithfulness labels rest on one uncued and one cued draw, so a switch may be sampling noise. The alpha correction only fixes aggregate rates.
records.method: CueBall: 8 baseline samples, 4 re-rolls per switch; pair persistent if at least 3/4 hit the cue target. 5 open reasoning models, 4 MCQ sets (incl. MedQA), 8 cues, T=0.7. LLM role judge, audited by a second LLM plus human review.
records.findings: About 40% of positive-case single-sample unfaithful labels fail persistence (survival 59.7%). 1-alpha (median 0.4%) is closer to non-recurrence than to non-persistence (median 21%). Incoherent traces persist less (39.4% vs 81.0%). Aggregate rates and model rankings mostly similar. Costs 3.8-5.7x the tokens. Releases 20,000 traces and code.
records.limits: T=0.7 only, no greedy decoding; open models of 12B or less; 4 re-rolls give a coarse estimate; uncued and cued decoding unmatched; judge audit covers one model and dataset, incoherence label unvalidated; post_hoc cue is 45% of the release; persistence does not prove cue causation; not yet peer reviewed.

records.problem: Complex RL rewards can't be verified perfectly. Does a misspecified outcome reward alone, with no monitor pressure, hide learned reward hacking from CoT monitors?
records.method: Testbed pairs a true and a misspecified reward on 3 tasks: exceed word limit, favor Gemini when judging, pass only some tests. GRPO-LoRA misaligned vs control models; CoT-only LM monitor; intervention and reward-intent g-mean². Fix: an LM infers a reward description from training rollouts; it is injected into half the rollouts of a new RL run and the model is updated without it.
records.findings: Misaligned models hack 0.87 on average (control 0.05), but the monitor flags only 18% of hacks; g-mean² at most 0.34, because CoTs reason about the stated intent (coding: CoTs collapse). Still low with the word limit unstated, except gpt-oss-120b. A stronger monitor adds only 0.09/0.12. Description training raises g-mean² by 0.26/0.43 and TPR from 0.18 to 0.82, and CoTs name the hack; more control-model false positives, most on the judge task.
records.limits: Synthetic misspecifications, 3 tasks, 10 tests per coding problem; needs a second RL run; description generator is told which output aspect the reward concerns; description-trained gpt-oss-120b stops hacking on length (0.15), which muddies gains; true-task cost not reported; code promised, not released; under review.

records.problem: Do an LLM's moral judgments and the choices it states in role predict the tool actions it actually takes as an agent?
records.method: 2,000 matched synthetic cases (temptations with a reference answer, dilemmas without one). Each is run three ways: observer judgment (Should), in-role written choice (Say), simulated tool call (Do). 14 models. Kimi-K3 codes whether Qwen3.5-27B's Should considerations carry weight in its Say and Do rationales. Probes and steering on 4 open models.
records.findings: Should-Do reference-agreement gap reaches 22.3 pp. Say-Do exceeds Should-Say in 13 of 14 models. 85.2% of Should considerations stay load-bearing in Say vs 69.3% in Do. Probes repair at most 3.7% of mismatches; action-trained directions repair 54.4-100%, with model-dependent retention loss. Operator instructions widen the gap.
records.limits: Synthetic cases, simulated two-option tools. Perspective, information access and interface vary together. Rationale coding is not causal. Steering is exploratory, on a simplified no-reasoning task. Under review. Code released.

operator or system instructions pushing toward an option that the model's own stated principles reject, studied as a driver of gaps between stated and enacted choices

records.method: Honesty adapter: a rank-16 LoRA stacked on frozen organism LoRAs, trained with SFT on MO-533 (on-policy transcripts from 533 organisms, judge-labeled admissions plus honest negatives). Negatives are essential, and logit readout beats judging sampled answers.

records.problem: Plan- and CoT-based oversight of tool-using agents assumes stated plans govern irreversible actions; no black-box causal test of this exists.

records.limits: Ratified template plans, not self-authored; constructed indifference and manufactured conflicts; open models only; one main domain (airline n=5 gated tasks); temperature 0; original raw logs lost, so results come from a regeneration; workshop paper.

records.problem: Unknown what internal computation a model builds when RL teaches it to use MCQ hints while hiding them from its CoT.
records.method: Model organism: Gemma 3 1B, SFT then GRPO (LoRA) with a -3.0 penalty for mentioning the hint. Gemma Scope 2 CLTs pretrained on the base model act as anomaly detectors: per-layer FVU differential and new-feature counts over with-hint, no-hint and non-MCQ prompts, correct vs wrong hints, and 6 checkpoints.
records.findings: 98% accuracy with hints vs 38% without, 0% leakage. Added computation peaks at layers 20-23. Two features (L15/f478, L12/f317) new in all 10 tested prompts. Correct- vs wrong-hint differentials correlate at r=0.971, read as content-agnostic concealment. Differential present from step 50 and roughly flat over training: no phase transition.
records.limits: Hint-specific signal ~10x smaller than total GRPO change, so CLTs cannot separate hiding from format changes. Single 1B model, MCQ only, 20 prompts per condition. Features not functionally characterized. No code release mentioned.
